mira: Heads upwe need to settle runtime checks for machine tokens. Proposal: machine tokens (machine_token) carry a small `caps` list; data plane only verifies signature + caps + scope. keep heavy role eval off hot path.

devin: sounds good. question: how do we handle one-off delegated ops where service must act as user?

chen: delegated tokens: mint a short-lived, single-use token via control plane. include `on_behalf_of` and `nonce`. runtime validates nonce by checking a small in-memory bloom filter or calling control plane for misses. keeps most calls local.

mira: revocation model: short TTL (5-15m) + emergency revocation list keyed by subject. services cache the revocation generation per subject. broker increments gen to revoke. cheap compare on hot path.

devin: migration: keep Authorization header compatible. console shows migration suggestions for keys that are machine-like. plan a 30-day opt-in followed by 10% header-gated enforcement, then 100%.

chen: security constraints: forbid `admin:*` in machine tokens except via explicit manual approval. require KMS signing for minting.

mira: telemetry: token_type, caps_count, validation_ms, revocation_hits. aim <1ms added latency using local JWKS and per-subject gen cache.

token-bot: Reminder created: "machine-token rollout sync"  2024-07-10T15:00Z.

devin: action items: mira prototyping validator lib (2w), chen revocation API + gen store (1w), devin migration heuristics + console text (5d).

mira: I'll write a short RFC with token shapes and validator pseudo-code. Drop any edge cases here.
